# Make sense of omics data

[← Main guide](../README.md) · [Browse resources](resources.md)

Choose a biological question and learn one analysis end to end. Bulk analysis, single-cell analysis, and other omics specialisms share foundations, but each needs its own experimental and statistical context.

<a id="bulk-rnaseq"></a>

## Sequencing and bulk RNA-seq

**Level:** Beginner

Connect read processing and quantification to sample-level statistical analysis.

**Before you begin:** Basic R or a Galaxy introduction; statistics and sample metadata.

### What to understand

- Read QC, alignment or quantification, references, and gene-level counts.
- Sample-level QC, design formulas, contrasts, and differential expression.
- Effect sizes, multiple testing, gene-set interpretation, and reporting.

### What you’ll be able to do

Produce a reproducible comparison with a clear design, QC plots, and an interpreted results table.

### Try this

Start with the count-based RNA-seq project. Then follow a full FASTQ-to-results tutorial to learn where those counts come from.

### Keep in mind

A count-based tutorial does not teach raw-read processing by itself. Keep normalization for visualization distinct from the model's input requirements.

### A few good resources

- [Bioconductor: gene-level RNA-seq workflow](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/workflows/html/rnaseqGene.html) — Workflow · Intermediate · Free · English. Connect RNA-seq processing with exploratory analysis and differential expression through a documented workflow.
  - Prerequisites: Basic R, sample metadata, and introductory statistics.

- [DESeq2 vignette](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Understand count-based differential expression, model design, contrasts, diagnostics, and interpretation.
  - Prerequisites: R and experimental design.

- [Galaxy Training Network](https://training.galaxyproject.org/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Training free; server quotas vary · English. Hands-on biological analysis tutorials across sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and other domains.
  - Prerequisites: Choose an introductory pathway; many require no programming.

- [nf-core/rnaseq](https://nf-co.re/rnaseq) — Workflow · Intermediate · Code free; compute and storage may cost · English. A production workflow to examine after a smaller tutorial; learn its inputs, profiles, QC outputs, and documented options.
  - Prerequisites: RNA-seq concepts, Nextflow, and suitable compute access.

<a id="single-cell"></a>

## Single-cell RNA-seq foundations

**Level:** Intermediate

Learn the core workflow before adding integration or complex models.

**Before you begin:** R or Python, count matrices, and experimental design.

### What to understand

- Cell and sample QC, ambient RNA, doublets, and normalization.
- Dimensionality reduction, clustering, marker evidence, and cell annotation.
- Donor-aware comparisons, pseudobulk approaches, and differential abundance.

### What you’ll be able to do

Explain the evidence for an annotation and the experimental unit for a comparison.

### Try this

Follow one small tutorial in Scanpy or Seurat. Keep a table recording every filtering decision and inspect how one changed threshold affects the result.

### Keep in mind

Clusters are analytical groupings, and annotation requires biological evidence. Preserve donor metadata throughout the workflow.

### A few good resources

- [Single-cell Best Practices](https://www.sc-best-practices.org/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. A question-oriented reference for single-cell analysis across modalities, including preprocessing, statistics, and integration.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python or R and single-cell biology.

- [Scanpy tutorials](https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/index.html) — Tutorial · Intermediate · Free · English. Work through Python single-cell analysis examples and inspect how preprocessing decisions affect downstream results.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python and single-cell matrices.

- [Seurat guided clustering tutorial](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/pbmc3k_tutorial.html) — Tutorial · Intermediate · Free · English. An R entry point to single-cell QC, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and marker exploration.
  - Prerequisites: Basic R and single-cell concepts.

- [AnnData documentation](https://anndata.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Understand the annotated matrix structure used in many Python single-cell workflows, including observations, variables, and layers.
  - Prerequisites: Python and basic single-cell matrices.

<a id="integration"></a>

## Dataset integration and scvi-tools

**Level:** Advanced

Address technical differences while checking that meaningful biological variation is retained.

**Before you begin:** A complete single-cell workflow, covariates, and batch-effect concepts.

### What to understand

- Integration across datasets versus integration across molecular modalities.
- Reference mapping, batch covariates, latent representations, and scVI/scANVI.
- Evaluation of biological conservation alongside technical mixing.

### What you’ll be able to do

Justify an integration strategy and describe how you checked its consequences.

### Try this

Compare an unintegrated baseline with one integration method. Inspect known biological groups and sample composition as well as a low-dimensional plot.

### Keep in mind

A well-mixed embedding is not sufficient evidence of a good integration. Confounded study designs can make technical and biological effects difficult to separate.

### A few good resources

- [scvi-tools tutorials and model guides](https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/stable/) — Documentation · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. Choose probabilistic models by task and modality, and read their assumptions alongside the worked tutorials.
  - Prerequisites: Python, single-cell analysis, and statistics.

- [Single-cell Best Practices](https://www.sc-best-practices.org/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. A question-oriented reference for single-cell analysis across modalities, including preprocessing, statistics, and integration.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python or R and single-cell biology.

<a id="multiomics"></a>

## CITE-seq and multimodal analysis

**Level:** Advanced

Relate RNA, protein, and chromatin measurements while respecting how they were collected.

**Before you begin:** Single-cell foundations and basic integration concepts.

### What to understand

- CITE-seq RNA and antibody-derived tags; protein background and modality-specific QC.
- Paired versus unpaired measurements, missing modalities, and MuData.
- totalVI for RNA–protein data and MultiVI for RNA–chromatin accessibility data.

### What you’ll be able to do

Choose a method whose assumptions match the modalities and pairing in the experiment.

### Try this

Follow the totalVI CITE-seq tutorial. Compare RNA and protein evidence for selected markers and document cases where they disagree.

### Keep in mind

Multi-omics is broader than single-cell RNA–protein analysis. Describe each modality and its measurement process before selecting an integration tool.

### A few good resources

- [totalVI: RNA and protein analysis](https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/stable/user_guide/models/totalvi.html) — Guide · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. A model guide for joint RNA–protein analysis, with links to CITE-seq examples and discussion of the observation model.
  - Prerequisites: CITE-seq concepts, Python, and single-cell QC.

- [MultiVI: RNA and chromatin accessibility](https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/stable/user_guide/models/multivi.html) — Guide · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. Study joint RNA–chromatin accessibility modeling, including the paired and unpaired data setting.
  - Prerequisites: Single-cell RNA/ATAC concepts and Python.

- [MuData documentation](https://mudata.scverse.org/latest/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Understand how multimodal observations and modality-specific matrices are organized and linked.
  - Prerequisites: Python and AnnData.

- [Single-cell Best Practices](https://www.sc-best-practices.org/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. A question-oriented reference for single-cell analysis across modalities, including preprocessing, statistics, and integration.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python or R and single-cell biology.

<a id="perturbations"></a>

## Single-cell perturbation analysis

**Level:** Advanced

Study how cells respond to genetic, chemical, or environmental interventions.

**Before you begin:** Single-cell foundations, experimental controls, and sample-level inference.

### What to understand

- Perturb-seq design, guide assignment, controls, and perturbation efficacy.
- Differential expression, differential abundance, and heterogeneous responses.
- Observed-response analysis versus prediction of unseen responses; held-out evaluation.

### What you’ll be able to do

Define an appropriate comparison and explain what a model evaluation does and does not test.

### Try this

Use a Pertpy tutorial to compare perturbations with controls. Record replicate structure, guide assignment choices, and the intended generalization task.

### Keep in mind

Random cell-level splits can fail to test the generalization you care about. Design evaluation around held-out donors, conditions, or perturbations as appropriate.

### A few good resources

- [Pertpy: perturbation analysis](https://pertpy.scverse.org/en/stable/) — Tutorial · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. Explore guide assignment, perturbation efficacy, response comparisons, and prediction through documented examples.
  - Prerequisites: Single-cell analysis and experimental design.

- [Single-cell Best Practices](https://www.sc-best-practices.org/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. A question-oriented reference for single-cell analysis across modalities, including preprocessing, statistics, and integration.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python or R and single-cell biology.

- [scvi-tools tutorials and model guides](https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/stable/) — Documentation · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. Choose probabilistic models by task and modality, and read their assumptions alongside the worked tutorials.
  - Prerequisites: Python, single-cell analysis, and statistics.

<a id="immune-repertoires"></a>

## TCR, BCR, and immune repertoires

**Level:** Advanced

Connect immune receptor sequences, clonotypes, and cellular phenotypes.

**Before you begin:** Basic immunology and single-cell data handling.

### What to understand

- V(D)J sequences, chain pairing, productive receptors, and clonotype definitions.
- Clonal expansion, diversity, overlap, and sampling depth.
- Linking repertoire information to RNA expression and cell states.

### What you’ll be able to do

Explain a clonotype definition and distinguish clonal relationships from evidence of antigen specificity.

### Try this

Complete a Scirpy tutorial and compare two reasonable clonotype definitions. Report how the interpretation changes.

### Keep in mind

Receptor similarity or clonal expansion alone does not establish shared antigen specificity. Document sequence and grouping criteria.

### A few good resources

- [Scirpy: immune receptor analysis](https://scirpy.scverse.org/en/latest/) — Tutorial · Advanced · Free · English. Learn repertoire QC, clonotype analysis, and integration of receptor information with cell-level measurements.
  - Prerequisites: Python, single-cell data, and basic immunology.

- [AIRR Community documentation](https://docs.airr-community.org/en/stable/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Use community terminology, data standards, and metadata guidance when handling receptor repertoire datasets.
  - Prerequisites: Basic adaptive immune repertoire concepts.

<a id="other-omics"></a>

## Other omics and directions to explore

**Level:** Intermediate

Keep the wider field visible while choosing a tractable next specialization.

**Before you begin:** Biological data literacy and statistics.

### What to understand

- Variant analysis, genome annotation, and reference-dependent interpretation.
- Proteomics and metabolomics: experimental platforms, quantification, and data processing.
- Spatial omics: tissue context, spatial dependence, and assay-specific analysis.

### What you’ll be able to do

Choose a specialization and find an introductory workflow appropriate to its data.

### Try this

Choose one Galaxy learning pathway and map its raw data, processing stages, biological question, and outputs.

### Keep in mind

This is an orientation to additional fields, not a complete curriculum for each one. Use the specialist training materials for detailed methods.

### A few good resources

- [Galaxy Training Network](https://training.galaxyproject.org/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Training free; server quotas vary · English. Hands-on biological analysis tutorials across sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and other domains.
  - Prerequisites: Choose an introductory pathway; many require no programming.

- [EMBL-EBI on-demand training](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/on-demand) — Course · Beginner · Free · English. Find focused introductions to biological databases and analysis areas, including routes into additional omics fields.
  - Prerequisites: Vary by course.

- [Ensembl training](https://training.ensembl.org/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Learn to navigate genome annotation, identifiers, comparative data, and Ensembl tools using worked training materials.
  - Prerequisites: Basic genetics.

- [Single-cell Best Practices](https://www.sc-best-practices.org/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. A question-oriented reference for single-cell analysis across modalities, including preprocessing, statistics, and integration.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python or R and single-cell biology.
